editor.modeExplainer: Interview mode is one of the workspace interaction modes, alongside Chat and Code, picked from the mode selector in the chat panel. In it you choose a template like this one, and the agent works through your items as a conversation, generally one at a time. It cannot finish until every required item is covered.
editor.artifactExplainer: It records what it learns into an artifact: a Markdown notes file under /.interviews/. The interview agent reads the whole project freely but can only write inside that one folder, so an interview never changes your actual files. Turning those notes into real work is a separate step, which you can offer as a one-tap handoff (below).
editor.titleHelp: Name it by what it produces, like the built-ins: “Understand a company”, “Plan a feature”. Shown in the picker.
editor.descPlaceholder: e.g. Turn an idea into a buildable plan for a site: its purpose, audience, pages, and the action it should drive.

editor.artifactHelp: The artifact: the Markdown file this interview writes its findings into. Give it a meaningful name. Must live under /.interviews/ and end in .md.
editor.itemsHelp: Each item is one thing to gather. The question is what to learn from the user; the “done when” criteria is the checkable condition the completion check reads the artifact against. Order the items the way the conversation should flow.
editor.questionPlaceholder: e.g. The pages or main sections the site needs (home, about, services, contact)
editor.questionHelp: What to gather, not a literal script. The agent asks it in its own words, and can inspect the project first (e.g. “check what is already there with ls”).
editor.criteriaPlaceholder: e.g. The artifact lists the pages or main sections the site needs
editor.criteriaHelp: A checkable statement about the artifact. Phrase it as “The artifact records / lists / describes ...”. A model reads the artifact and decides if this is met.

editor.handoffHelp: Optional. A convenient way to let the user act on the result right away. Enable it to show the user a button, once the interview finishes, that starts a normal generation from what was recorded, without retyping anything. For example, the built-in “Plan a website” interview offers “Build this site”, which hands its site plan to the agent to build from. Configure the button below.
editor.handoffLabelHelp: The text on the button shown when the interview finishes.
editor.handoffPromptPlaceholder: e.g. Build the website described in /.interviews/site-plan.md
editor.handoffPromptHelp: The message sent to the agent when the user taps the button. Reference the artifact path so it reads what the interview recorded.

pricing.description: A pricing comparison section with 2-4 plan tiers shown as cards. Each card has a plan name, price, feature list, and CTA button. One tier is usually highlighted as recommended.

faq.name: FAQ
faq.description: A frequently asked questions section with expandable/collapsible question-answer pairs. Typically uses an accordion pattern.

cta-banner.name: CTA Banner
cta-banner.description: A call-to-action banner with a headline, short supporting text, and one or two action buttons. Often has a contrasting background color.

text-block.name: Text Block
text-block.description: A content block with a heading and one or more paragraphs of body text. May include inline links and basic formatting.

image.name: Image
image.description: An image element with optional caption and alt text. Can be inline, full-width, or sized to fit its container.

video.name: Video
video.description: An embedded video player, either a hosted video file or an embed from YouTube/Vimeo. Includes playback controls and optional poster image.

card.name: Card
card.description: A card component with an optional image, title, description, and action link/button. Contained in a bordered/shadowed box.

list.name: List
list.description: An ordered or unordered list of items. Each item may have an icon, title, and description. Can be styled as a simple bullet list or a more complex item list.

button.name: Button
button.description: A clickable button element. Matches the site’s existing button styling.

form.name: Form
form.description: A general-purpose form with labeled input fields, validation, and a submit button. Field types determined by context.

contact-form.name: Contact Form
contact-form.description: A contact form with name, email, subject, and message fields plus a submit button. May include validation and a success message.

search-bar.name: Search Bar
search-bar.description: A search input with a search icon/button. May include autocomplete suggestions or a dropdown of results.

modal.name: Modal
modal.description: A modal/dialog overlay triggered by a button or action. Contains content, a close button, and optional action buttons in a footer.

table.name: Table
table.description: A data table with headers, rows, and columns. May include sorting, pagination, or filtering. Responsive on smaller screens.

chart.name: Chart
chart.description: A data visualization chart (bar, line, pie, etc.). Includes labels, a legend, and sample data. Type determined by context.

stats-counter.name: Stats Counter
stats-counter.description: A row of statistic counters showing key metrics (e.g., "10K+ Users", "99.9% Uptime"). Each stat has a large number and a label below it.

progress-bar.name: Progress Bar
progress-bar.description: A horizontal progress indicator showing completion percentage. Includes a label, percentage text, and a filled bar segment. Can be single or stacked for multiple metrics.

metric-cards.name: Metric Cards
metric-cards.description: A row of dashboard-style KPI cards. Each card shows a metric label, a large value, and an optional trend indicator (up/down arrow with percentage change). Commonly used in admin panels and dashboards.

data-list.name: Data List
data-list.description: A vertical list of key-value pairs displayed in rows. Each row has a label on the left and a value on the right, separated by a divider. Used for settings pages, profile details, or specification sheets.

sidebar-nav.name: Sidebar Nav
sidebar-nav.description: A vertical sidebar navigation panel with grouped links, icons, and optional section headers. Can be collapsible. Typically fixed on the left side of an application layout.

breadcrumbs.name: Breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.description: A horizontal breadcrumb navigation trail showing the current page location within a hierarchy (e.g., Home > Products > Category > Item). Each level is a clickable link except the current page.

tabs.name: Tabs
tabs.description: A tabbed interface with a row of tab buttons and a content area below. Clicking a tab shows its associated content panel. One tab is active at a time. Includes tab labels and optional icons.

pagination.name: Pagination
pagination.description: A page navigation control with numbered page buttons, previous/next arrows, and an indicator of the current page. Used below lists, tables, or grids of content to navigate between pages of results.

accordion.name: Accordion
accordion.description: A series of collapsible content panels. Each panel has a clickable header that expands or collapses its body content. Unlike FAQ, this is a general-purpose container for any grouped content that benefits from progressive disclosure.

gallery.name: Gallery
gallery.description: A grid or carousel of images with optional captions. Supports a lightbox view for full-size viewing. Can display as a uniform grid, masonry layout, or horizontal scrolling carousel with navigation arrows.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.description: A vertical timeline showing a sequence of events in chronological order. Each entry has a date/time marker, a title, and a description. Connected by a vertical line with dots or icons at each event.

profile-card.name: Profile Card
profile-card.description: A card displaying a person or team member. Includes an avatar/photo, name, role or title, a short bio, and optional social media links or a contact button.

login-form.name: Login Form
login-form.description: A login form with email/username and password fields, a submit button, a "forgot password" link, and optional social login buttons (Google, GitHub, etc.). May include a "remember me" checkbox and a link to a registration page.

file-upload.name: File Upload
file-upload.description: A file upload area with a drag-and-drop zone and a browse button. Shows selected file names, sizes, and upload progress. Supports single or multiple files with optional file type restrictions.

notification.name: Notification
notification.description: A toast or banner notification component for displaying messages to the user. Includes an icon, message text, and a dismiss button. Supports variants: success, error, warning, info. Can auto-dismiss after a timeout.

dropdown-menu.name: Dropdown Menu
dropdown-menu.description: A button that opens a floating menu of actions or options. Menu items can have icons, dividers between groups, and optional keyboard shortcuts. Closes on selection or clicking outside.
